name: Web Speech recognition
meaning: Uses the microphone to transcribe speech. In Chrome the audio is sent to a Google service by default, so spoken words leave the device unless on-device recognition is chosen.

web.api: new webkitSpeechRecognition() or SpeechRecognition; recognition.start(); processLocally; SpeechRecognition.available(); install()

access.prompt_ui: Microphone prompt on first start(); Chrome shows the mic indicator; on-device mode needs a downloaded language pack.
steps: result events carry transcript text and confidence

limits.headline: Can turn your spoken words into text while you speak and the tab is open
limits.user_action: You click the microphone or Dictate button and allow the microphone
can: Turn your speech into text as you talk
Use the words to fill a box, search or run a voice command
Work on the device itself in Chrome when the language pack is downloaded
cannot: Start without the microphone prompt on first use
Listen after you stop or leave the tab
Keep your audio private in Chrome by default; audio may go to a speech service unless on device mode is used
Work in Firefox, and only partly in Safari and iPhone browsers
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet support it fully. Safari and iPhone browsers support part of it. Firefox does not.

story.what_it_is: Turns what you say into text, using your microphone.

marketing.name: SpeechRecognition
marketing.pitch: Developer docs describe how a page can turn spoken words into text, with limits on which browsers support it.

story.for_you: You allow the microphone, then speak, and your words appear as text or trigger a command. In Chrome, your voice is usually sent to a Google service to be turned into words, so it leaves your device.
story.for_makers: Voice typing and voice commands make forms, search and games hands free. A maker gets a speech feature without training a model. The cost is that voice audio often goes to a third party cloud, which is a privacy and legal question.

use_cases.example: A person with a hand injury dictates a whole email with their voice and sees the words appear in the draft.
A word game or trivia site lets you shout your answer instead of typing it, and the page checks the words.
A reading practice site listens as a child reads aloud, and highlights words they say right or wrong.
You say a note or a to do item into a web app, and it saves the words in a list.
You say a product name into a store search bar instead of typing, and results appear.
A video call tool turns speech into live captions for people who are deaf or in a noisy place.
A web dashboard for your home lets you say turn on the lights and sends the command.

risks: Spoken words may go to a cloud service
Always listening mode can hear private talk

technical_bounds: Cloud processing by default in Chromium

history.change: processLocally and install() for on-device models (exact version unconfirmed)
